nodes.label: ADR-001 — App scope: embroidery-focused block app
nodes.rationale: A full Pocket Code port exceeds bachelor-project scope, but a blocks-free drawing tool would lose Catrobat's learn-to-code essence; so the brick set is restricted to exactly the subset embroidery needs (motion, control/loops, variables/formulas, the eight embroidery bricks) with stage preview and DST export. Brick parity is defined against the Android embroidery bricks, not all of Pocket Code.

nodes.label: ADR-002 — Stack: native Swift 6 / SwiftUI, engine as SPM package
nodes.rationale: Catty is dated (UIKit+SpriteKit, Obj-C/Swift mix, iOS 13) and Catrobat plans a Flutter port; native was reconfirmed anyway because the thesis assignment is a modern native standalone iOS app. Platform-independent engine in an SPM package gives a TDD-friendly `swift test` loop without a simulator. Cost: diverges from the org's Flutter direction, so maintenance stays a separate native track.

nodes.label: ADR-003 — Project format: native JSON first, .catrobat later
nodes.rationale: `.catrobat` ZIPs with a quirky versioned code.xml are heavy early effort; a Codable/JSON format with a version field keeps the model close to Catrobat concepts (scene/object/script/brick/formula) so an importer can be added later. DST stays the only interoperability requirement in core scope.

nodes.label: ADR-004 — Minimum iOS version 17.0
nodes.rationale: Trade device coverage against modern SwiftUI APIs: iOS 17 covers the vast majority of active devices and unlocks the Observation framework, avoiding pre-Observation state-management workarounds.

nodes.label: ADR-005 — DST semantics ported from Catroid, verified against Catty fixtures
nodes.rationale: Two references exist; Catroid is the canonical semantic source of truth (512-byte header, 3-byte records, jump 0x80, color-change 0xC0, max 121 units/stitch, pixel-to-unit factor 2.0, terminator 00 00 F3) while Catty ships real golden files. Port concepts, not code — everything is AGPL-3.0. Engine tests are written against known-good bytes before implementation exists.

nodes.label: ADR-006 — App-layer architecture: @Observable MVVM, no TCA
nodes.rationale: TCA was explicitly evaluated and rejected: solo thesis developer, five-hour stories, handover to a non-TCA org, and the test-critical complexity already lives in the pure SPM package. Three TCA-inspired patterns are adopted without the framework — a pure `EditAction` enum through one `apply(_:)` funnel, initializer-injected side-effect interfaces with deterministic doubles, and editor tests asserting the whole `Program` value. Undo/redo is a bounded in-memory snapshot stack, never persisted.

nodes.label: ADR-007 — Stage coordinate space and physical units
nodes.rationale: Stage size determines the physical embroidered size (1 pt = 2 DST units = 0.2 mm), bounded by real ~100x100 mm consumer hoops, and the convention is baked in long before any UI exists. Center origin, y-up, fixed 500x500-point virtual stage; the engine applies no y-flip (matching both references) — flipping is purely an M3 rendering concern. Angles in degrees with 0 = up (x via sin, y via cos), Catroid convention.

nodes.label: ADR-008 — Script representation: flat brick list with paired control bricks
nodes.rationale: A nested-tree model would force multi-week custom nested drag-and-drop in SwiftUI, whereas a flat list maps onto List + .onMove with free reorder, VoiceOver reorder actions and swipe-to-delete. Nesting is rendering (indentation), not model structure. Clarified during US-203: a moved pair travels as a complete balanced block, so reinsertion anywhere nests rather than splits — the move primitive accepts every in-bounds destination and rejects only ill-formed moves.

nodes.label: ADR-009 — Stage rendering: SwiftUI Canvas with batched paths
nodes.rationale: Catty's one SKShapeNode per stitch is a known SpriteKit performance trap at tens of thousands of stitches; Catroid batch-renders with one ShapeRenderer. Metal-backed SwiftUI Canvas strokes one Path per colour run, settled stitches rasterise to a cached image and only the live tail redraws. Zoom/pan is a CGAffineTransform so the math is unit-testable, and the renderer sits behind a protocol to keep a Metal escape hatch open.

nodes.label: ADR-010 — Device family: universal, iPhone-first
nodes.rationale: Catrobat's school context makes iPads common and editor-beside-stage is the natural iPad layout; deciding in M6 would mean rebuilding the navigation skeleton, so M3's skeleton is size-class adaptive from the start (compact sequential, regular split).

nodes.label: ADR-011 — Privacy: fully offline, no accounts, no tracking
nodes.rationale: Audience is largely minors (13-18) with GDPR-K/COPPA and age-rating implications; no network, accounts, analytics or tracking removes consent UX entirely, simplifies App Store review and is a selling point for schools. Only egress is the user-initiated share sheet.

nodes.label: ADR-012 — DST semantics: Catroid authoritative, known Catty divergences not ported
nodes.rationale: The references disagree at byte level and Catty's golden fixture is self-golden (origin-start, positive-quadrant, single-colour-boundary only), so Catroid wins wherever they diverge and fixtures must be viewer-verified before a golden test is trusted. Pins CO = colour blocks starting at 1, the interpolation sequence, rounding as floor(x+0.5) with round-then-subtract deltas, magnitude-only extents relative to the first stitch, workspace dedup, and a do-not-port list of Catty bugs (rejecting legal ±121, 16-char name, signed extents, 4-point sew-up). One deliberate divergence from Android: Set Thread Color emits a colour change when the new colour actually differs.

nodes.label: ADR-013 — Color-change flag placement on interpolated moves; documented flag transposition
nodes.rationale: Catty consumed a pending colour flag on the first interpolation jump (old position), Catroid applies it to the target before interpolating so it lands on the final plain stitch. The sewn output is identical (jumps sew nothing) but the bytes are not. Catroid placement wins because the deciding concern is the Catroweb workflow — a shared program must produce the same DST bytes on iOS as on Android — so the color_change.dst golden is compared through a documented two-byte transposition (C3→83, 03→C3) asserted inside the test.

nodes.label: ADR-014 — Pattern-layer arithmetic is Double; sub-resolution float divergence accepted
nodes.rationale: Catroid computes patterns in Java float; the engine uses Double, and sin/cos residue (~1e-16) makes Catroid's integer-exact expected coordinates unassertable with ==. Last-ulp divergence is orders of magnitude below embroidery resolution and is absorbed by javaRound, so pattern tests assert within 1e-9 absolute tolerance. Deliberate divergences from Catroid: degenerate-input guards (zero/negative length, non-finite inputs emit nothing) avoid porting a NaN-poisoning accident Swift would turn into a trap; headings are normalized mod 360 exactly; updates whose stitch count exceeds 1,000,000 emit nothing rather than saturating or trapping. Bit-exact parity with Android is explicitly not guaranteed.

nodes.label: ADR-015 — Set Thread Color emission semantics
nodes.rationale: Neither reference decides three edges, so they are pinned: a colour set before the first emitted stitch is silent (no phantom leading block, consistent with Catroid's precedent that changes only enter non-empty streams); invalid hex is a full no-op mirroring SetThreadColorAction exactly, down to UTF-16 code-unit offsets and Java's Character.digit set; clause-B transition points are black because DSTWorkSpace never assigns a colour; and exactly ±121 units on a layer switch follows the reference's strict > / < operators, whose opposite argument order makes the clause distance and the stream's interpolation check disagree at half-unit gaps.

nodes.label: ADR-016 — M2 target layout: ProgramModel and Interpreter as two sibling targets
nodes.rationale: A single combined target would make every model import transitively pull in the engine, but M4's editor and M5's persistence need neither stitch machinery nor DST types. So ProgramModel is Foundation-only (positions as Doubles, colours as hex Strings) and Interpreter is the only place model and engine meet. The dependency DAG stays a straight line inward and ProgramModel's engine-freedom is enforced at build level rather than by convention; cost is one more target plus the interpreter owning all model-to-engine conversions.

nodes.label: ADR-017 — Formula arithmetic is native Double; decimal128 divergence pinned
nodes.rationale: Catroid evaluates PLUS/MINUS/MULT/DIVIDE in BigDecimal DECIMAL128; native Double diverges by ~1 ulp per operation, an absolute bound that catastrophic cancellation or a tiny divisor can make arbitrarily large relative to the result, so no universal tolerance exists and tests assert selected cases at pinned magnitudes. Mirrored rather than diverged: non-finite normalization, zero-divisor DIVIDE to NaN, interpretInteger truncation with Int32 saturation, the POW NaN guard, and POW zero-sign canonicalization. Pinned divergence: non-finite Double literals normalize at the leaf where Catroid's string-typed NUMBER nodes would coerce to 0 — an accepted public-API divergence.

nodes.label: ADR-018 — Interpreter tick and clock semantics
nodes.rationale: Verified against Catroid's ThreadScheduler/ScriptSequenceAction/RepeatAction/WaitAction and libgdx SequenceAction/TemporalAction. Compilation is one-shot to a linear instruction array with backpatched loop indices; a tick is one round-robin pass with exactly one action-producing instruction per thread; loop bookkeeping is zero-tick and folds into the completing tick. wait uses an accumulating logical clock, not wall-clock, and accumulation is authoritative even when binary FP drifts one tick from the nominal ceil. The interpreter never halts — every bad-formula path continues with a per-brick Catroid fallback — which is why M3's run enum has no failed case. Two degenerate cases (empty repeat loops detecting termination one tick late, compounding under nesting) are characterized rather than fixed because the fix would cost the common nested-loop entry case.

nodes.label: ADR-019 — Structure-determining threshold crossings are a distinct class from coordinate tolerance
nodes.rationale: A stitch pattern decides how many stitches an update emits by floor(distance/length); at a whole multiple that comparison sits on a rounding boundary and one ulp of hypot changes the emission structure, which a 1e-9 coordinate tolerance cannot express. The deciding test is not 'is the distance on a boundary' but 'how far is the exact distance from it in ulps', measured on the along-motion component of the floating-point residue — US-207's square is on the boundary but its residue is purely perpendicular (~3e-31 margin) while US-208's star sits 1.878e-15 below 20, outside the half-ulp, so only Darwin's 0.53-ulp-high hypot yields four intervals. A golden whose structure depends on such a crossing must document it and guard it with a direct tripwire assertion, not a comment.

nodes.label: ADR-020 — The engine's coordinate boundary: encodable-delta trigger and guarded no-ops
nodes.rationale: Two coordinate traps: the interpolation decision measures a rounded stage difference while the encoder subtracts individually rounded positions, so javaRound's asymmetry lets a 121-measured move encode as 122 and trip a precondition (a released-app crash); and Int(javaRound(v*2)) traps on non-finite and out-of-range values. The encoded delta becomes a second interpolation trigger but never a second split count (count stays Catroid's ceil, or 2 when only the encoded delta triggers, because a one-way split would not terminate). Recursion termination additionally requires the stage lattice step to stay within ±121 units per axis, scoped per axis and measured at the coarsest step inside the interval. EmbroideryPoint.init(converting:) becomes failable so the trap is unrepresentable; rejection is a guarded no-op that keeps pending flags armed and does not re-anchor. Left open deliberately: DSTHeader field-width traps, specified as US-211.

nodes.label: ADR-021 — M3 preview data path: colour-resolved stitch events into an append-only display list
nodes.rationale: InterpreterEvent.stitch carried no colour while assembledStream() resolves it, and three data paths were possible but not equivalent. The event gains a colour supplied by a read-only EmbroideryPatternManager.threadColor(for:), the app accumulates into an append-only StitchDisplayList with incremental colour runs, bounds and a settledCount watermark, and assembledStream() is called once per run for the export model only — a structural reason, not a speed one, since it keeps the engine sole owner of ADR-015's colour semantics.

nodes.label: ADR-022 — M3 target layout: Samples and StagePreview as app-support targets
nodes.rationale: Sample builders lived only in test targets and SwiftPM forbids test-target-to-test-target dependencies; and the exit criterion 'zoom/pan transform math is unit-tested' decides where that math lives — inside the package it runs under swift test and the pre-commit gate, inside the app it needs a simulator. So Samples (ProgramModel only) and StagePreview (Foundation-only, Double-based transform math) join the package, which grows from three library targets to five and stops being purely 'the engine' — accepted because the alternative puts an exit-criterion test behind a simulator boot.

nodes.label: ADR-023 — What runs where: local gate protects engine semantics, CI protects the app
nodes.rationale: The engine's swift test is 1.4 s for 489 tests; anything booting a simulator costs tens of seconds and would fall on every commit in a small-commit process. So the local gate compiles (build-for-testing, signing-free) but never runs the app, and cannot catch a runtime failure — a stated limit, since app failure modes are layout/navigation/wiring that CI catches before merge. The durable result is abandoning command-text parsing: five consecutive Codex rounds each found a hole in the previous round's regex at rising severity, so the gate now asks `git status --porcelain` instead. The local gate is a convenience, not an enforcement boundary — required status checks on main are.

nodes.label: ADR-024 — The stage renderer: batching hoisted out of the renderer
nodes.rationale: Batching becomes a value (StitchDrawPlan) rather than renderer logic — forced, because a double conforming to StagePreviewRenderer records that protocol's inputs and never has a path list, and the alternatives were a GraphicsContext spy (forbidden, it defeats the Metal escape hatch) or a double that asserts itself. The plan holds indices, never geometry, so a pan or zoom cannot invalidate it. Deliberate deviations from both references: traversals drawn distinctly with a dashed chrome colour (the machine trims travel, so travel is not design data, and a shape difference survives Increase Contrast); every display-list entry dotted; dots stroked last; colour-run boundaries suppress the segment. The dark-mode rule narrows to 'inside the canvas everything is fixed, outside everything is semantic', because thread colours are design data and an adapting field would make the same design invisible in one appearance.

nodes.label: ADR-027 — The run lifecycle: two tasks, a terminal that cannot be forgotten, three budget axes
nodes.rationale: Both references get the stop path wrong in the same direction — Catty tears down the object graph its own shareDST reads, Catroid anti-throttles up to 50 act() calls per frame against its own O(n) rebuild — and neither is ported. There are necessarily two tasks and stop() cancels only the producer, because only the producer can observe cancellation and emit the terminal update; cancelling the consumer stops the run and silently loses the export model. RunTermination carries a non-optional exportModel funnelled through one private terminal(), making 'the terminal batch always carries assembledStream()' a type rather than three code paths that each remembered. Three budget axes are kept distinct: ticksPerFrame throttles, maxStitchesPerFrame ends a frame but never a run, maxStitchesPerRun is the only producer of stitchLimitReached.

nodes.label: ADR-028 — Zoom and pan: one commit per gesture, a fit-aware floor, a transition-only summary
nodes.rationale: SwiftUI gesture values are cumulative from the gesture's start, so per-callback folding compounds them; committing once in onEnded is correct and also makes 're-rasterise on gesture end' structural rather than timed. The zoom floor is a rule (min(fit.scale, minimumScale)) not a constant, because fitting floored lower than pinching could reach. The accessibility summary is written only on run-state transitions, enforced by a separate RunPhase type since private(set) inside PreviewRunState would still let apply(_:) write every frame. Three corrections are carried: the mid-gesture design was reversed after Sebastian found defects visible only during a gesture (stills-based definitions of done cannot catch them), the interaction layer was rewritten rather than patched a seventh time after six flat-Medium review rounds found one conceptual mistake in four spellings, and two rewrite claims (idempotence as ownership, the fit animation becoming a snap) were themselves wrong. Generalisable lesson: to know whether something is happening, ask the thing, not its output.

nodes.label: Catroid (Pocket Code Android) reference implementation
nodes.rationale: Canonical embroidery implementation (org.catrobat.catroid.embroidery) and the arbiter wherever the two references disagree at byte level.

nodes.label: Catty (Pocket Code iOS) reference implementation and golden fixtures
nodes.rationale: Swift prior art plus the self-golden stitch.dst / color_change.dst fixtures; trusted as goldens only after viewer verification, and carrying a documented list of byte-level bugs that must never be ported.

nodes.label: javaRound — floor(x + 0.5) rounding rule
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Java Math.round and differs from Swift's .rounded() on negative halves; its asymmetry is the root cause of the ADR-020 interpolation-vs-encoder disagreement and of ADR-015's opposite-argument-order clause distances.

nodes.label: E1 — Infrastructure epic
E2 — Embroidery engine epic
E3 — Program model & interpreter epic
E4 — Stage & preview epic
E5 — Block editor epic
E6 — Projects & persistence epic
E7 — Export & sharing epic
E8 — Release readiness epic
S* — Stretch epic (freehand paths, .catrobat import, SVG plotting)
M1 — Engine core milestone
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-07-16, US-101–US-110. Exit criterion: a generated DST loads correctly in an embroidery viewer and matches golden-file expectations for header, records, jumps, colour changes and terminator.

nodes.label: M2 — Interpreter MVP milestone
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-07-31, US-201–US-210. Exit criterion: a hardcoded square/star program produces the expected stitch stream in unit tests and the interpreter is incrementally consumable — step-by-step consumption yields the same stream as batch execution, with an injected clock for time-based bricks.

nodes.label: M3 — Walking skeleton app milestone
nodes.rationale: Pick a bundled sample, run it with live stage preview, export DST via share sheet — proving the full thread through all layers. Exit criteria: end-to-end sample→preview→DST, a synthetic 50k-stitch design at 60 fps on A15-class hardware, and unit-tested zoom/pan transform math (met without a simulator because StagePreview is a Foundation-only target). The run enum's `failed` case was removed as having no producer, since ADR-018 guarantees the interpreter never halts; failure belongs to the export lifecycle.

nodes.label: M4 — Block editor milestone
nodes.rationale: Tap-to-add palette matching Catroid's flow rather than free-form drag; parameter editing is type-specific and a full Catroid-style formula keyboard is deferred so no editor surface is built for functions the M2 interpreter lacks. Ends with an informal usability session with 3-5 target-age users via TestFlight.

nodes.label: M5 — Project management milestone
M6 — Brick parity & polish milestone
nodes.rationale: Polish is an audit, not a build-out, because the M3+ definition of done keeps states, accessibility and strings continuous. Parity target is listed as a checklist early so M6 is not discovering scope.

nodes.label: Engineering standards (Swift Testing, strict concurrency, Bundle.module fixtures)
nodes.rationale: Swift Testing not XCTest; tests run in parallel so no shared mutable state or fixed file paths; Swift 6 strict concurrency from day one with Sendable value types and a synchronous isolation-agnostic engine core, leaving actor/@MainActor decisions to the app layer.

nodes.label: Definition of done for UI stories (M3+)
nodes.rationale: No hardcoded user-facing strings (String Catalog, leading/trailing layout for ~75 languages incl. RTL); loading/empty/error states ship with the feature; animations respect Reduce Motion; a VoiceOver pass with the stage canvas summarising stitch count, colours and size in mm; 44 pt touch targets; Dynamic Type to AX1 without truncation.

nodes.label: Backlog mechanism — analysed-but-unscheduled stories
nodes.rationale: Stories are written up at discovery time rather than left as journal carry-forwards, so a closed milestone's 'all N stories merged' claim stays true and the analysis is captured while fresh. Precedent: the ±121 coordinate trap sat as a carry-forward from 2026-07-09 to M2 planning and was mis-scoped twice by review before becoming US-210. The mechanism proved itself with US-211, whose answer changed once M3 planning gave it a real caller.

nodes.label: Milestone 1 story set overview (~35 h, ten stories)
nodes.rationale: Every story is developed test-first; ADR-012 is the arbiter where the references disagree, and the tightest estimates (US-103, US-106) carry their own mitigations — a verbatim conversion-table port and a hex-diff test helper.

nodes.label: US-101 — Project scaffold, SPM package and CI
nodes.rationale: The point of the story is the pipeline, not the code: a failing lint or test must fail CI, verified by pushing a deliberately failing commit. The toolchain version is pinned because runner-default drift breaks Swift 6.x builds, and the Catty fixtures are viewer-verified here because they are self-golden files that US-104/US-106 will build golden tests on.

nodes.label: US-102 — Stitch domain model and embroidery stream
nodes.rationale: One shared representation for all pattern generators and the DST writer. EmbroideryStream is a plain Sendable struct with mutating appends — Catty's class + SynchronizedArray + draw-queue design is deliberately not ported, because M3's preview only needs 'stitches since index i', which an array gives for free.

nodes.label: EmbroideryStream (stitch accumulation and metadata)
nodes.rationale: Exposes stitch count, colour-change count, bounding box and first/last stitch positions precisely because the DST header's ST, CO, extents and AX/AY derive from them with no caller-supplied redundancy. It is also the single writer, owning interpolation, dedup and pending flags, which is why stitch patterns return positions instead of writing into it.

nodes.label: US-103 — DST stitch record encoder
nodes.rationale: The 243-entry table is ported verbatim as data rather than hand-deriving the encoder from the bit diagram, because the algorithmic derivation is where the estimate would blow up. The decoder lives in the test target only — no product feature reads DST in M1–M6.

nodes.label: CONVERSION_TABLE (243-entry Tajima record table)
nodes.rationale: Ported verbatim from Catroid's DSTFileConstants with a provenance comment (AGPL-compatible), covering deltas within ±121 inclusive — Catty's strict-comparison guard rejecting legal ±121 is a bug and is not ported.

nodes.label: US-104 — DST header writer
nodes.rationale: Exactly 512 ASCII bytes with NUL-padded numeric fields, LA truncated to 15 chars (Catroid's rule, not Catty's 16), CO = colour changes + 1, and extents relative to the first stitch as magnitudes only. Golden tests use concrete literal inputs so the story does not depend on interpolation; a non-origin first-stitch test covers what the fixtures cannot.

nodes.label: US-105 — Long-move interpolation and jump handling
nodes.rationale: The algorithm is pinned to the reference implementations rather than cleanly reimplemented, because US-106 requires byte-identical golden output. Emission order is duplicate-of-P as jump, evenly spaced intermediates as jumps, Q as jump, then Q again as a plain stitch; splitCount = ceil(maxAxisDistance/121) with intermediates rounded in stage coordinates before unit conversion.

nodes.label: US-106 — DST file generator with golden-file verification
nodes.rationale: The milestone exit criterion. Golden-test failures must report the offset and hex context of the first mismatching byte — byte-diff debugging without that helper is where days go. The primary API returns in-memory Data so tests stay parallel-safe; the write-to-URL convenience is a thin wrapper tested against a unique temp URL.

nodes.label: US-107 — Running stitch pattern
nodes.rationale: Patterns receive position and heading — not the movement vector — because zigzag and sew-up derive geometry from the needle's heading, and the two differ under goto/glide. Patterns are pure state machines returning stitch positions so the stream stays the single writer and patterns test without a stream. Two types mirror Catroid: a lifecycle wrapper (activate/pause/resume/stop) and the pattern state machine it delegates to.

nodes.label: StitchPattern protocol and NeedleUpdate
nodes.rationale: `mutating func update(_: NeedleUpdate) -> [StagePoint]` — amended from returning [Stitch] because Stitch carries converted embroidery units plus jump/colour flags, all of which belong to the stream rather than the pattern.

nodes.label: US-108 — Zigzag stitch pattern
nodes.rationale: The anchor is passed explicitly because the engine is platform-independent and cannot read a sprite's position. The heading is sampled once per update call — Catroid does not re-orient within an update, so a new heading takes effect on the next one. The angle-convention mapping is documented in the tests because it is the classic silent-flip bug source.

nodes.label: US-109 — Triple stitch pattern and sew-up
nodes.rationale: SewUp is Catroid's 5-point centre/ahead/centre/behind/centre sequence, not Catty's 4-point variant. The dedup interaction is made explicit by test: if the needle just stitched at the sew-up's centre, dedup drops the first centre point and 4 records are emitted, matching Catroid — the single-actor slice of the dedup rule landed here to make that test executable.

nodes.label: US-110 — Thread color changes and layer assembly
nodes.rationale: Owns the workspace dedup rule's actor/layer/colour dimensions and the layer manager assembling streams in z-order with colour changes inserted between layers, mirroring DSTPatternManager's TreeMap-of-layers behaviour. Emission semantics were refined at close-out by ADR-015 (silent start, invalid-hex no-op, clause-B black, ==121 tie-off).

nodes.label: Dual-driver workflow plan (Claude Code / Codex CLI interchangeable)
nodes.rationale: Parked design. Driving concern: a future maintainer after transfer to Catrobat may not have a Claude subscription and should be able to drive the same TDD/ADR-arbitrated workflow with Codex, with Claude flipping into the reviewer role, without losing the test gate, formatting or subagent delegation. Research on the installed Codex CLI v0.144.0 found the 'Codex has no hooks/subagents' assumption outdated, so genuine feature parity — not just documentation parity — is achievable. No mode switch: both toolchains live in the repo permanently and a maintainer simply runs whichever CLI they have. Treated as tooling, so it gets no ADR.

nodes.label: Shared hook scripts (scripts/hooks, scripts/review)
nodes.rationale: Pull the logic currently inlined as one-liners in .claude/settings.json into standalone scripts (test-gate.sh, format-swift.sh, cross-vendor-review.sh) so both vendors' hook systems call the same code rather than drifting apart.

nodes.label: Codex CLI primitives (.codex/config.toml hooks, .codex/agents, .agents/skills)
nodes.rationale: Codex CLI's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks share Claude's matcher/command/exit-code-2 schema and trust-on-first-use model; project-scoped agents are TOML files with sandbox_mode; skills use the same open SKILL.md frontmatter format Anthropic authored and OpenAI adopted. Same delegation boundary applies on both sides — no test-creator, no TCA agents, no modernizer.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md parity rule
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md is today a reduced document that drops the hook mechanics and subagent roster; it must gain them back and be framed as the Codex-as-driver mirror. A process-rule change to CLAUDE.md has to be mirrored in the same session, called out explicitly because AGENTS.md was already found silently out of sync once on 2026-07-10.

nodes.label: Append-only journal rule
nodes.rationale: Rule from Sebastian 2026-07-10: entries are never edited or amended because the unrevised record — including mistakes and wrong first attempts — is the thesis methodology data. Corrections are new dated entries referencing the old one.

nodes.label: Codex cross-vendor review loop (/codex-review)
nodes.rationale: Automated 2026-07-09 as a command plus a PR-creation hook: an adversarial-semantics pass from a different vendor, deliberately complementary to swift-code-reviewer's rubric. Findings are triaged against the ADRs, which win over the reviewer, and the verdict is recorded in the PR description. Repeatedly found defects the in-loop reviewer missed, and repeatedly found defects in the *previous round's own fixes*.

nodes.label: Review-loop convergence stop rule (cap became a convergence test)
nodes.rationale: A fixed round count ended loops while findings were still arriving (US-302 round 5), so the rule became: stop when a round produces no code changes, or when severity has fallen for two consecutive rounds. A flat-severity run is not convergence — flat or rising severity for three rounds escalates, which is exactly what happened to ADR-023's command classifier and to US-307's interaction layer, where the answer was to abandon the approach rather than patch it again.

nodes.label: Pre-commit test gate and [red] marker
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse hook runs the engine tests before any git commit and caught two real bugs immediately. Deliberate TDD red-phase commits carry a literal [red] marker so CI shows the red baseline — an escape hatch, not a lock, since anyone can bypass their own pre-commit hook.

nodes.label: Agent roster mapped to workflow phases; delegation boundary
nodes.rationale: Delegate verification and retrieval liberally, generation only against a complete spec. Story tests are never delegated — they encode the ADR-012/013 byte semantics and are the least delegable work in the repo; swift-engineer may implement a green phase against already-red tests. TCA agents are out of scope per ADR-006 and swift-modernizer has nothing to modernize in greenfield Swift 6.

nodes.label: Ink/Stitch manual viewer verification
nodes.rationale: The only check no automated layer performs: a generated .dst opened in a real embroidery viewer. It established fixture trust before goldens were built on them, traced a square gap to a moving colour-change record, and twice disagreed with a golden where the viewer's own arithmetic turned out to be wrong.

nodes.label: Planning-time buildability check on story test plans
nodes.rationale: Introduced after US-305 planning found an unbuildable test plan in a story that had already survived three review rounds. It paid for itself three consecutive stories: US-306 had two criteria that would have failed silently, and US-307 had six criteria that could not be built as written — two already green from an earlier story, one vacuous, one unassertable, and two mutually contradictory.

hyperedges.label: M1 DST export pipeline (model → records → header → interpolation → file)
The Double-arithmetic divergence policy (tolerance, thresholds, coordinate bounds)
M3 preview stack (data path, target layout, renderer, run lifecycle, interaction)
